plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 based on prior iteration evidence. Three complementary routes proposed: (1) Tight bound-constrained optimization per feedback directive with ±15% thickness bounds around baseline QW values and interior-point solver; (2) Return to 20-layer topology which achieved highest prior score (0.978) with relaxed bounds to allow more exploration; (3) Alternative material pair PbSe/ZnS for potentially lower absorption in target IR range while maintaining high index contrast. All routes preserve the Ge/ZnS or equivalent high-contrast dielectric Fabry-Perot cavity principle validated in prior rounds.

routes.title: Ge/ZnS 24-Layer with Tight ±15% Bound Constraints and Interior-Point Solver
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Constraining layer thicknesses to ±15% of quarter-wave baseline values (550±82.5 nm for Ge, 900±135 nm for ZnS) while using an interior-point optimizer that penalizes large inter-layer thickness ratios will improve optimization convergence and maintain the coherent half-wave stacking foundation, yielding target scores comparable to or exceeding prior 24-layer results (0.960).
routes.design_principle: Trust-region optimization around verified baseline preserves the physical cavity resonance structure while allowing localized impedance tuning. Tight bounds prevent the optimizer from exploring physically unrealistic thickness combinations that degrade spectral performance.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | CaF2 substrate. Total 24 finite layers with alternating Ge/ZnS sequence starting with Ge.

routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer alternating Ge/ZnS multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate under normal incidence from air ambient. Layer sequence: Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS (24 finite layers total). Initialize all Ge layers at 550 nm with optimization bounds [467.5, 632.5] nm. Initialize all ZnS layers at 900 nm with optimization bounds [765, 1035] nm. Use coherent TMM solver across wavelength range 3600-5200 nm. Optimize for four objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4150-4350 nm band, maximize mean transmittance in 4550-4750 nm band, minimize mean transmittance in 3600-4000 nm band, minimize mean transmittance in 4850-5200 nm band. Use interior-point or trust-region optimizer that penalizes large inter-layer thickness ratios. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Implements feedback directive: tight ±15% bound constraints around baseline QW values with interior-point solver to preserve coherent half-wave stacking while permitting localized impedance tuning.

routes.title: Ge/ZnS 20-Layer Fabry-Perot with Relaxed Bounds Based on Prior Best Performance
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing layer count from 24 to 20 while maintaining the alternating Ge/ZnS Fabry-Perot cavity structure will recover the higher target scores observed in iteration 05 (0.978), as fewer layers reduce optimization complexity and cumulative fabrication tolerance effects while still providing sufficient stopband rejection.
routes.design_principle: The 20-layer configuration achieved the highest prior target score (0.978) compared to 24-layer variants (0.960, 0.811). Fewer layers reduce the dimensionality of the optimization problem and may allow the optimizer to find better solutions within the same computational budget.

routes.title: PbSe/ZnS 24-Layer Alternative Material Pair for Reduced Absorption
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Replacing Ge with PbSe as the high-index material while retaining ZnS as low-index material will reduce absorption losses in the 4.1-4.8 μm target bands, potentially improving peak transmittance while maintaining sufficient index contrast for effective Fabry-Perot cavity formation.
routes.design_principle: Ge exhibits non-negligible absorption in the mid-IR range which may limit peak transmittance. PbSe has lower absorption coefficient in the 4-5 μm range while maintaining high refractive index (~4.5-4.7), potentially enabling higher peak transmittance with similar layer count.
